“O Syama! I worship Your mountainous playgrounds, Govardhana, Varsana, and Nandagrama, which like valuable gems set in the golden ornament of Vraja hang on the neck of fortunate goddess Bhumi.

“Where is that pious soul who will not bathe in the sacred waters of Vrndavana, like Radha-kunda and the Yamuna, waters that not only wash away sinful reactions but bestow the gift of love for You?

“O Hari! When will Bilvavana, which is always full of ripe *bel* fruit, reveal to me the vision *of gopas* excitedly playing ball with fallen fruit while servant boys busily make fruit juice for Your pleasure.

“O sons of Nanda! When will I walk through dense Bhandiravana, where You herd cows, where the ground is littered with gems, and where birds, like Vedic scholars, endlessly discuss Your divine glories?

“O Lord of Bhadravana, Balabhadra, whose splendour eclipses the full moon, whose strength supports the universes, and who always carefully protects His younger brother from harm, I bow before You.

“On the bank of the Yamuna in Lohavana, a young boatman once waited in an old boat. O Radha! Be careful! That boatman will raise His fare before reaching the far shore. Are you prepared to pay Him?

“In Mahavana one can hear the sound of cows lowing, yogurt being churned, and victimised cowherds yelling, ‘Catch the thief and tic Him up!’ O Radha and Syama! May these sounds one day fill my ears.

“O Sridama! I often remind Krsna that you are still waiting for Him in Bhandiravana. When He finally comes to you, will you reward my thoughtfulness by reminding your sister that I wait for Her mercy?

“O Radha! O Syama! Darlings of the Vraja-vasis! The happiness of family life holds no attraction for me, and yet I long to be welcomed into Your spiritual family of happy cowherd men and women.

“I hope to bow at the feet of Mother Yasoda and Nanda Maharaja, to worship the effulgence of their toenails, compared to which the *brahmajyoti* that the Mayavadis seek is hardly as bright as a candle.

“If I could only see Subala and Sridama in a joyful wrestling match with the two sons of Nanda, in which the stakes are each other’s lunch packs, then all my austerities will have borne a sublime fruit.

“Within my heart of hearts I long to receive a nod of recognition from *gopis* like Lalita or Rupa as they leave their homes in the morning to wake and dress Radha for Her excursion to Nandagrama.

“O Caitanya-candra! O unlimited ocean of love for Krsna. Will my endeavours to serve Your mission in this life move Your heart enough to one day transform me into an official resident of celestial Vraja?

“Dear Srila Prabhupada! Your unlimited kindness has transformed my life from a quicksand of hopeless despair into a nectar ocean of sublime spiritual aspirations, some of which I have just revealed.

“You are a miracle worker. That Sivarama Swami, descendent of the Hunas, chants Krsna’s name is one miracle. That New Vraja-dhama, an oasis in the desert of Kali-yuga, appeared in Hungary is another.

“Why should I not have faith that you will work yet another miracle? Will I one day, by your grace, enter that divine realm where the pastimes retold in this book eternally occur and you eternally reside?

“If you are inclined to bestow your causeless mercy upon this poor soul, then please also bestow it upon your followers who, with steady hearts, chant Lord Krsna’s holy names and serve your divine mission.

“Although this request may seem unnecessary, especially in light of your standing promise that we will go back to Godhead, I repeat it to give me inspiration to persevere until my final breath in this world.

“O land of devotees, New Vraja-dhama! Please, without reservation, bestow your mercy upon those who till your soil, walk your paths, pick your flowers, and worship your two Lords, Radha and Syama.

“I conclude my prayers by offering respectful obeisances to all the Vaisnava devotees of the Lord — be they great or small — who are just like desire trees, for they can fulfil the desires of this lowly soul.”

**\* \* \* \***

I made my way to Visrama-ghata, where I offered prostrated obeisances to Krsna’s abode. After smearing the dust of New Vraja-dhama all over my body, I waded into the Yamuna to take a full bath.

Offering respects to the *dhama* and to the divine couple who reside there, but unable to say that my *parikrama* was complete, I set out for the temple to fill my eyes with the superb vision of Radha and Syama.

I had walked through all the sacred forests, bathed in holy waters, and remembered the transcendental pastimes corresponding to each divine place. Why did I feel my *parikrama* was not yet complete?

Because I had hoped for more! Was I a dreamer? For my *parikrama* to be truly complete, I felt I would have to step into unmanifest Vraja, the one seen only by spiritual eyes. But, alas! I had not.

Still, I had no reason to lament! For although I could not say that my *parikrama* was complete, I did not feel lacking in any way. Chanting Krsna’s names and remembering His pastimes is always satisfying.

These are two marvelous attributes of devotional service: in any stage — practice, ecstasy, or perfection — *bhakti-yoga* is always complete, and yet service to Krsna constantly seeks to expand itself.

As a result, while devotees — even up to Srimati Radharani Herself— always feel satisfaction by serving Krsna, at the same time they feel themselves unworthy and eager to increase their Krsna consciousness.

Walking along the cobbled road, I recalled how the Lord had once told Narada that the nature of His mercy, devotion, and love is that no matter how much of it devotees have, they always want more.

Although devotees always strive to increase their devotion by emulating the serving mood of another, they are happy to serve Krsna in their unique ways, thus expanding the mosaic of spiritual variety.

As I recalled the rest of the dialogue between Krsna and the sage Narada, a conviction filled my heart: Radha and Syamasundara were leading me on to a more satisfactory conclusion to my *parikrama.*

Narada had requested Krsna’s permission to distribute the news of the Lord’s pastimes in his travels, and for the blessing that those who heard his words would be qualified with pure love for the Lord.

My conviction reflected a perspective deeper than my own. It came spontaneously and, in my humble estimation, from the unending nature of the mercy that Narada Muni and the Lord spoke of.

This realisation exposed the true conclusion of my *parikrama,* two nectarean fruits that became increasingly more relishable as I contemplated their significance, for me as well as for others.

The two fruits of my *parikrama* were the realisations of how the blessings Krsna had given Narada relate to me as a servant of Radha-Syama, a resident of New Vraja-dhama, and a preacher in Hungary.

These two fruits reinforced my mission in Hungary. They were nothing new, nothing earth-shattering, but they were of significance to me because of my conviction that they had come from Krsna.

And when I tried to verify this realisation with my intelligence to determine whether it was also what Srila Prabhupada would want from me, the answer was an immediate and unhesitating yes.

Dear readers! Allow me to share my thoughts on how Narada Muni’s two requests of the Lord defined my final prayer to Radha and Syama and my service to New Vraja-dhama and to the Hungarian *yatra.*

After having travelled from Prayaga to Dvaraka and having met all kinds of perfected devotees, Narada found that the objects of Krsna’s greatest mercy were the Vraja *gopis.* In ecstasy he petitioned the Lord:

*Payam payam vraja-jana-gana-prema-vapi-marala sriman-namamrtam aviratam gokulabdhy-utthitam te*  
*tat-tad-vesacarita-nikarojjrmbhitam mista-mistam sarvau lokan jugati ramayan matta-cesto bhramani*

**“O swan gliding in the lakes of the Vraja-vasis’ love! I wish that I may wander everywhere always chanting and drinking the nectar of Your names. Those most sweet names arise from the ocean of Gokula —**

**“And spread the glories of Your infinitely varied dress and ways of acting. As I wander, behaving like a madman, may I distribute joy to everyone in all the worlds.”**

Desiring a second boon, Narada asked —

*Tvadiyas tab kridan sakrd api bhuvo vapi vacasa hrda srutyangair vd sprsati krta-dhih kascid api yah*  
*sa nityam sri-gopi-kuca-kalasa-kasmira-vilasat-tvadiyanghri-dvandve kalayatu-taram prema-bhajanam*

**“Whether by speaking, thinking, hearing, or physical contact, if any person in this world comes in touch even once with these pastimes of Yours and is convinced of their importance —**

**“May he be endowed eternally with the power to worship Your feet in pure love, feet resplendent with the saffron dust from the pitcher like breasts of the blessed** ***gopis.”***

In summary, Narada requested that he may always sing the praises of Yasoda’s son, and that faithful people who hear such songs may he awarded with loving devotion to Krsna in the wake of the Vraja-vasis.

My service and desires for Hungary — with New Vraja-dhama as the spiritual capital and Radha and Syama as its residents’ worshipable Deities — felt very much the same as Narada’s desires for the universe.

Thus I offered my final prayer: “O playful children of the kings of Vrndavana who, like a white and a black swan, ply the waters of Your worshippers’ devotion! Please hear this lowly person’s humble plea.

“Permit me to reside in and always return to Your abode of bliss, New Vraja-dhama, and from there let me wander the length and breadth of this land carrying the order of Srila Prabhupada on my head.

“My mind always fixed on Your lotus feet, let me chant the supreme mantra of Your names and praise Your glories from the immortal works of poets like Vyasadeva, Rupa Gosvami, and Srila Prabhupada.

“Let the nectar cascading from Your names as I perform *sankirtana* quench my own craving for Your company, bless devotees with transcendental bliss, and free the common man from worldly illusion.

“Their bonds of material attachment made loose, their devotional practices made to rein in their turbulent lives, let devotees taste the divine joy that makes one laugh, cry, and dance like a madman.

“When they are freed from illusion and savour transcendental reality, may their faith progressively sprout and blossom beneath the shower of *nama-sankirtana* and the benediction rays of the Caitanya sun.

“As they gradually distinguish between the names, forms, and qualities of various incarnations of the Lord, they will conclude that supreme bliss, sweetness, and devotion are to be had only in You.

“Beloveds of the residents of Vraja! May my words clearly and transparently convey Srila Prabhupada’s teachings on *vraja-bhakti,* and may those who hear them receive them with corresponding faith.

“Inspired by You from within, may all sincere souls come to New Vraja-dhama to share in or to embrace the bliss of life in Vrndavana, in which You, Radha and Syamasundara, are the life-giving source.

“Then they will see how insignificant the nectar of honey is compared to the nectar found in Your smiles, and how the taste of sugar is hitter compared to the sweetness of Your faces and forms.

“Observing Your servants, wandering Your land, honouring their daily practices, devotees will taste the unique sweetness that only being connected with You — or things connected to You — can bring.

“By direct perception, devotees’ faith will unfold and within their hearts the unflinching determination will take root: ‘I must make Radha and Syama the centre of my life and the goal of my devotions.’

“O enchanting couple! With Your smiles as my wings, let me be a songbird that sings to my countrymen of Your names, forms, and pastimes, luring them to surrender to You in New Vraja-dhama.

“Having now heard my first request to be Your empowered emissary, O You who are called *sva-danatrpta,* ‘Those never satisfied with Their own charity,’ please hear my second and final plea.

“In whomever awakens faith in the truth of Your names and pastimes, by steady hearing and remembrance may those devotees attain the purity of heart to regain their birthright to love You like Vraja-vasis.

“O crown jewels of the treasure chest of New Vraja-dhama! Devotees eager to hear about You from Your representatives will naturally become attracted to this land as their own place of pilgrimage.

“Whether they come to reside here or whether they regularly visit, those devotees will serve You by developing Your abode, supporting Your worship, and seeing the places where You perform pastimes.

“To those pious souls who steadily serve You in a regulated way, please give the gift of spontaneous attraction to Your Vraja-vasi companions and to the Vraja-vasis’ special manner of serving You.

“When that attraction arises and devotees become fully absorbed in thoughts of You, may the power of Your names and pastimes endow them with the love of God of which Srila Prabhupada always spoke.

“The fulfilment of these desires would complete my ambition in this life: that I act as a catalyst for Your names and pastimes to transform, like a veritable philosophers’ stone, lovers of sin into lovers of God.

“As for me, having seen the forests, water, hills, and pastures where You mercifully enjoy Yourselves, I shall constantly remember Your transcendental pastimes. Indeed, I shall never be able to forget You.

“How could I, when You have not only cleverly stolen my heart with Your lotus eyes, honeyed smiles, and blissful forms, but also left the impressions of Your lotus feet within my mind? It is not possible.

“And when, like all mortals, I must change this body for another, may my mind always take shelter of Your lotus feet, my tongue always be chanting Your names, and my body always be engaged in Your service.

“Since the time I once decided to somehow or another invoke Your mercy, I have repeated a verse Nanda Maharaja once spoke to Uddhava and the other cowherd men of Vrndavana.

“I have personalised this prayer in order to express my own sentiments for You. Please forgive me if, in comparing my sentiments to those of the topmost devotees of the Lord, I have committed any offence.

“Keep me in New Vraja-dhama for a hundred births or send me where You will, hut,

*karmabhir bhramyamananam yatra kvapi vam icchaya*  
*mangalacaritair danai ratir no radha-syamayoh*

**“‘Wherever I am made to wander about in this world by Your will, in accordance with the reactions to my fruitive work, may my good works and charity always bring me love for Radha and Syama.’**

“I conclude my *parikrama* in the same way all acts are brought to perfection, by chanting Your names. Hare Krsna, Hare Krsna, Krsna Krsna, Hare Hare / Hare Rama, Hare Rama, Rama Rama, Hare Hare.’’

## Appendix 30

***Were the Kanya-kumaris the Reborn Sages of Dandaka Forest?***

*(This appendix follows from the introduction to the pastime of Krsna’s stealing the clothes of the young unmarried gopis at Cira-ghata as it is described in chapter twenty five.)*

It is sometimes suggested that the young *gopis* whose clothes were stolen by Krsna, as described in *Srimad-Bhagavatam,* had previously been the sages of Dandaka forest whom Lord Rama had blessed to have Krsna as their husband. Since neither *Srimad-Bhagavatam* nor its commentators confirm this assertion, I was curious to see whether there were other sources that did.

In short, if any such authoritative statements exist, I was unable to find them. Rather, the evidence of both scriptures and *acaryas* is that the *vraja-kumaris* identified in *Srimad-Bhagavatam* are eternal associates of the Lord and followers of Dhanya-gopi. They are *nitya-siddhas,* not *sadhana-siddhas,* and could therefore not previously have been sages striving for perfection.

Moreover, the history of the Dandaka sages is described at length in *Sri Garga-Samhita,* wherein their encounter with Lord Ramacandra and their later birth as *gopis* both appear. For the purposes of this appendix I will narrate the history of the sages’ birth as *gopis:*

During the time of Krsna’s Vrndavana pastimes, the Dandaka sages took birth in East Bengal as the daughters of a noble and affluent cowherd by the name of Mangala who was the master of nine hundred thousand cows. Mangala Gopa had five thousand wives and by each wife he had one daughter that was beautiful, well mannered, and chaste. He lived happily until one day his cows were stolen and he suddenly found himself a pauper.

Mangala was detached from worldly enjoyment. Nonetheless he was sad that now he could not properly feed his young daughters and that in the future he would have no hope to get them married. While Mangala was lamenting his fate an elderly *gopa* called Jaya, who was on pilgrimage from Mathura, visited Mangala’s home and informed him of the fabulous wealth of Maharaja Nanda. Mangala carefully considered what he had heard and then sent his beautiful daughters to Nandaraja, requesting that Vraja’s king find the girls homes where they would be cared for and protected.

Magnanimous king that he was, Nanda Maharaja placed the girls in the best families, where they were treated exactly like begotten daughters and even dressed in silks and gold jewelry. The girls dutifully performed household chores and milked the family cows. When they first saw Krsna, memories of their previous births as sages in Dandaka forest awoke in them, as did their ardent desire to have Krsna as their husband.

In their lives as sages the girls were worshippers of Gopala, so when they had first seen Lord Rama they could understand that He was the object of their worship, hut in a greenish form. Now, as *gopis,* the sages finally saw their cloud-blue Gopala face to face.

One day Yamuna-devi appeared before the girls and offered to give them a benediction. Naturally, they begged that Krsna become their husband, to which the goddess replied, “So be it!” The *Garga- samhita's* narration of this pastime concludes by saying:

*tah prapta vrndakaranye kartikyam-rasa-mandale*  
*tabhih sardham-hari reme suribhih surarad iva*

**“Later, in the month of Karttika, in the circle of the** ***rasa*** **dance, Lord Krsna enjoyed with them as King Indra enjoys with many heavenly girls.”**

There are three relevant points in this narration: (1) there is never any mention of the sages performing the Katyayani-vrata; (2) the girls do not take birth in Vrndavana; and (3) they attain perfection by *sadhana,* through which Yamuna-devi fulfils their aspirations.

These details contrast sharply with what *Srimad-Bhagavatam* and its commentators tell us about the *gopis* whose clothes were stolen by Lord Krsna. The *Bhagavatam* proclaims that the *kanya-kumaris* underwent the Katyayani-vrata. Jiva Gosvami says that those *gopis* all took their births directly in Vrndavana. Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura asserts that they were eternal associates of the Lord like Dhanya-gopi. And Jiva Gosvami writes that Vrnda-devi directed them in the execution of their vows.

By comparing the statements of *Sri Garga-Samhita* to those of *Srimad-Bhagavatam* and our *acaryas* one must conclude either that the *Garga-Samhita* speaks of another day of Brahma in which the sages-turned-gopis undergo the Katyayani-vrata or, more reasonably, that they are from this day of Brahma but different *gopis.* By the grace of Yamuna-devi, the Dandaka sages did attain Krsna’s shelter, but only at the time of the autumn *rasa* dance, not before.

There is only one piece of evidence sympathetic to the Dandaka sages’ possible affinity to the *vraja-kumaris:* the sages desired to “be like Sita,” or, in other words, they desired to be married to Rama. The *vraja-kumaris* prayed to be married to Krsna, so both groups of *gopis* share a hint of *svakiya-rasa.*

If we deem such evidence substantial, then we might argue that although the dominant *gopis* who performed the Katyayani-vrata were the followers of Dhanya, the sages-turned-gopis may have also been present with them.

Such an extrapolation has some potential. But since I have not found reference from any *acarya* to lend it credence, my conclusion remains that these are two separate groups of *gopis* who attained the *rasa* dance by different means. The Dandaka sages reborn as *gopis* did not perform the Katyayani vow, nor did they have their garments stolen by Lord Krsna.

## Appendix 31

***The Different Practitioners Who Became Gopis in Krsna's Pastimes***

*(This appendix follows from the introduction to the saradiya rasa dance in chapter twenty seven. By playing His flute, Krsna first calls* *Srimati* *Radharani and then other groups of gopis, amongst which are both the Lord’s eternal associates and souls who had achieved perfection through spiritual practice. These different categories of perfected souls are described in this appendix.)*

*Sri Garga-Samhita* lists the different categories of practitioners who in this day of Brahma attained perfection as *gopis* by associating with Krsna’s eternal companions. Most of these devotees fulfilled their long-cherished desire to meet with Krsna during the autumn *(saradiya) rasa* dance, while others met with the Lord during later *rasa* dances cither in the winter or spring. From the time of their first meeting with Krsna, until the Lord’s departure for Mathura, these *gopis* repeatedly enjoyed different pastimes with Him including dancing in the nocturnal *rasa* dance.

This appendix will examine these different categories of devotees — beginning with those *gopis* who first met Krsna at the *saradiya rasa* dance — and describe how they finally attained Krsna.

**The Gopis Who Were Formerly the Personified Vedas**

Once, in Svetadvipa, the personified *Vedas* were offering eloquent prayers to Lord Hari. Pleased with them, the Lord said, “You may ask any benediction from Me.”

The personified *Vedas* carefully considered what would be the best thing to ask for and concluded, “Dear Lord! Please reveal to us that form of bliss described by the *Puranas* as the cause of all causes.”

“So be it!” Lord Visnu said, and to fulfil their request revealed before the sages the divine realm of sweetness, Sri Vrndavana-dhama, complete with Govardhana Hill and the river Yamuna, grazing cows and playful *gopas.* Once His abode was manifest, the Lord showed His ultimate form of sweetness, Sri Krsna, surrounded by beautiful *gopis* enjoying the *rasa* dance with Him.

Again Lord Visnu asked, “Is there anything else you desire?” The personified *Vedas* replied, “Seeing You in this youthful form of a cowherd, as enchanting as a thousand Cupids, the desire to serve You in the manner of Your gopis has arisen in our hearts. Please therefore allow us to become *gopis* in Goloka.”

Pleased at this request, Lord Hari told the personified *Vedas:* “The next time Brahma takes birth, you will also take your births, on earth, in the district of Mathura, in Vrndavana. Then, on the full moon night of *sarat,* I will become your lover in the circle of the *rasa* dance. At that time you will attain perfection.”

Of course, the Lord’s prediction came to pass: the personified *Vedas* took birth as *gopis* in the families of saintly *gopas* in Vraja and, by seeing Krsna, they fell passionately in love with Him. To attain the prince of Vraja these *gopis* took shelter of Vrnda-devi, and by her blessings Krsna kindly accepted them as His maidservants in the *rasa* dance.

Thereafter these *gopis* became Krsna’s constant associates. It was they whom Krsna sent across the Yamuna at Pani-ghata to feed Durvasa Muni. They made the first crossing to reach Durvasa on the strength of Krsna’s *brahmacarya;* they made the second crossing to return home on the strength of Durvasa’s austerities.

The *gopis* could not understand how Krsna, who by that time had been their lover for years, could be a *brahmacari.* Neither could they understand how Durvasa, who had eagerly consumed all their cooked offerings, could be subsisting only on the juice of *durva* grass and nothing more.

Krsna explained to Sri Radha and the *gopis* that although He eagerly reciprocates their love, He is always transcendentally situated, free of desire and unaffected by contact with the modes of nature. Thus He is a *brahmacari.* Similarly, Durvasa accepted the feast the *gopis* had cooked although he had no desire to eat; indeed, he lived only by drinking *durva* grass juice.

In this way the *gopis* that had once been the personified *Vedas* attained Krsna as their lover and were enlightened by transcendental knowledge.

**The Gopis Who Were the Women of Mithila**

When Lord Ramacandra broke the bow of Lord Siva ' and married Sita-devi, many women of Mithila witnessed the heroic deed. Seeing the Lord’s beauty, they were struck by desire for Him. Later, while Rama was still in their city, these women once approached the Lord in a secluded place and revealed their hearts to Him. Lord Ramacandra told them of His vow to accept only one wife but promised that by the proper performance of *sadhana* they would take birth as *gopis* in Vraja at the end of Dvapara-yuga.

Naturally, the women wondered what austerities they should perform as part of this *sadhana.* Lord Rama told them, “With devotion go on pilgrimage, give charity, perform austerities, and follow the rules of purity.” Having faith in the Lord’s words, the women did as they were told. Sure enough, the process of pure devotion led Krsna as their husband. At the completion of their vow, Krsna personally appeared, stole the clothes of the *gopis* as they bathed, and made them stand naked before Him. After returning their clothes, Krsna promised to become their lover at some future time, a promise He fulfilled on the night of the *saradiya rasa* dance.

Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura says that the *gopis* whose clothes Krsna stole were eternally liberated, unmarried girls such as Dhanya. But the *gopis* who were once the women of Mithila were devotees who attained perfection through practice. The question arises as to when the women of Mithila appeared in Krsna’s pastimes.

There are two possible answers to this question.

The first possibility is that the Mithila women did not appear during the current day of Brahma, but in another. This answer seems to be supported by the following statement of Krsna in *Sri Garga- samhita:* “The day after tomorrow, on the Yamuna’s beautiful shore, I will enjoy with You a *rasa* dance that will fulfil all your desires.” This statement differs from *Srimad-Bhagavatam’s* account, in which the two pastimes — Krsna’s stealing the garments of the *gopis* and the *rasa* dance — are separated by almost two years, not a few days.

The second possible answer assumes that the *Garga-samhita’s* description of Krsna’s appearance refers to the current day of Brahma. If that were the case, we are duty bound to see if there are any reasonable ways that both Cakravarti Thakura’s statement and Krsna’s promise in *Sri Garga-samhita* can be interpreted to show that the Mithila women appeared during the present day of Brahma.

Cakravarti Thakura’s statement that the *gopis* whose clothes were stolen were eternally liberated and unmarried, such as Dhanya-gopi, can be taken to mean that there were others present who were not eternally liberated. This is a reasonable interpretation for the phrase “such as Dhanya-gopi.” If most of the *gopis* were liberated, which appears to be the case, it is not uncommon to define something by its dominant characteristic. For example, Krsna is always described as herding cows. But we know that amongst the cows there are also bulls, buffaloes, and even goats, though they are rarely if ever mentioned. Because the cows are the most prominent in terms of number and import, Krsna is said to herd cows.

It is also possible that when Krsna says He will meet the *gopis* “the day after tomorrow” He does not mean it literally, but rather “at some time in the future.” In fact, when Krsna left Vrndavana He told the *gopis* that he would return “the day after tomorrow,” only to return years later.

Accepting that the *Garga-samhita’s* description of the Mithila women becoming *gopis* refers to the present day of Brahma, the two contradictory statements as just interpreted can support that conclusion. Thus the Mithila women took birth as young *gopis* and joined the associates of Dhanya to perform the Katyayani-vrata, and they too later met Krsna in the *rasa* dance.

**The Gopis Who Were the Women of Kosala**

After Lord Ramacandra had smashed the pride of Parasurama, He returned to the land of Kosala and His own city of Ayodhya with His new bride. Even though the women in the land of Kosala knew that Sita would be Rama’s only wife, many of them were determined to have the Lord as their husband; thus they went to the banks of the Sarayu to perform austerities.

Knowing these women’s hearts, Lord Rama also blessed them to become *gopis.* Indeed, to encourage them in their determination He spoke in a disembodied voice while they performed austerities by the river: “At the end of the Dvapara-yuga, in a forest by the Yamuna River, your desires will be fulfilled.”

These women of Kosala thus took birth in Vraja in the homes of the Upanandas and were later married to different *gopas.* But like the other girls of their age, the *gopis* who had been women of Kosala fell in love with Krsna, thinking that their youth, beauty, and grace were wasted on their husbands.

Sometimes Krsna would stop these girls on the paths of Vraja and tease them by tugging on their garments or joking with them. These girls were so absorbed in thinking of Krsna that when they went to market to sell yogurt, instead of calling out “Yogurt! Yogurt!” they would say “Krsna! Krsna!”

These *gopis* saw Krsna in all aspects of the creation and thus they remained always Krsna conscious. As a result, they displayed many exalted symptoms of ecstasy that evade even *Paramahamsas.* Eventually they abandoned everything family life and society had to offer and ran to Krsna for the *rasa* dance. While dancing alongside many other millions of *gopis*, the girls who were once women of Kosala placed their arms upon Krsna’s shoulders and became His surrendered servants.

The women of Kosala loved Krsna and thus their austerities yielded a result that neither *yoga, sankhya,* pious deeds, or religious rituals can award. By love and devotion they conquered Krsna, the Supreme Lord, who is otherwise unconquerable.

**The Gopis Who Were the Women of Ayodhya**

Like the women of Kosala, many women of Ayodhya who constantly saw Ramacandra in their city also abandoned all hopes for material happiness in pursuit of the Lord of their hearts. And like the Kosala women, they also performed austerities and achieved Krsna’s company, but not by taking birth in Vraja.

The women of Ayodhya took birth in the palace of King Vimala, who lived in his capital city, Campaka, in the province of Sindh. King Vimala was a great devotee and had been instructed by the sage Yajnavalkya to give his daughters in marriage to the son of Vasudeva in Mathura.

When his daughters came of marriageable age, the king sent a messenger to Mathura to find Vasudeva’s son. But the messenger was told that Kamsa had killed all of Vasudeva’s sons and only a daughter survived. Disappointed, the messenger began the journey home to his king. On the way, he saw Krsna herding cows by the Yamuna. The messenger was captivated by the Lord’s beauty; although he did not know who the cowherd boy was, His appearance fit the description of Vasudeva’s son. Thus the messenger returned to Campaka City with mixed feelings.

The messenger told King Vimala both the disappointing news that Vasudeva’s sons had all been killed and the fact that he had seen a mysterious cowherd boy who matched the description of Vasudeva’s son. What was King Vimala to do?

Just at that time the great devotee and warrior Bhisma was passing through the Kingdom of Vimala. After having appropriately received his guest, the king asked the grandfather of the Kurus for his advice, explaining everything that had happened since he had first received Yajnavalkya’s order.

King Vimala said, “Yajnavalkya Muni told me that the Supreme Lord would take birth as the son of Vasudeva and Devaki in Mathura and that I should offer my daughters to Him in marriage. My messenger has informed me, however, that Vasudeva has no living sons. What then should I do? To whom should I offer my daughters?”

“O King!” Bhisma replied. “Your future son-in-law is alive and well in Vrndavana, living incognito as a cowherd. When He is eleven years old He will go to Mathura, kill Kamsa, and rid the world of its troublesome demons. Lord Ramacandra blessed your daughters, and they are destined to be the consorts of Sri Krsna. Do not waste any time, but offer your daughters to Him.”

Overjoyed at this news, King Vimala at once sent his messenger to Vrndavana to invite Krsna to come and accept his daughters in marriage. The messenger joyfully returned to the shore of the Yamuna, where he again found Krsna herding cows.

Approaching the Lord in a secluded place, the messenger offered beautiful prayers and then relayed King Vimala’s request, saying, “O Lord! To please You, King Vimala has performed many sacrifices, generously given charity, performed austerities, served *brahmanas,* and chanted sacred mantras. His lotus-like daughters, purified by many vows, have long waited to have You as their husband. Considering all this, we request that You purify Sindhudesa with Your presence and accept Your devotee’s daughters as Your wives.”

Sri Krsna was very pleased by this request. After making sure that none of His friends were watching, in an instant He transported Himself and the messenger to Campaka. Krsna appeared there just as King Vimala was performing a sacrifice. The Lord descended from the sky, resplendent in all sweetness, and Vimala stood up in order to fall at Krsna’s feet.

First the king greeted the Lord, offering Him a seat on the royal throne in the presence of *brahmanas,* advisors, and the people of the city. Then King Vimala offered all of his possessions to Krsna. Seeing Vimala’s many daughters looking at Him from the palace windows, Krsna smiled at them and then told the king, “O noble-hearted one! I am here because of the words of Yajnavalkya. Ask a boon from Me.”

Hearing this, the king replied, “O Lord of lords! I have only one desire and shall never have another. Please make my heart a bumblebee always tasting the nectar of Your lotus feet.”

The king then offered His daughters to Krsna in a grand marriage ceremony. As the spectators shouted “Jaya! Jaya!” and the demigods showered flowers, he offered the Lord respectful obeisances.

In the presence of all who watched, the king attained a spiritual form resembling Krsna’s. Along with his wives, Vimala climbed onto the hack of Garuda and returned to the spiritual world.

At last Krsna took responsibility for Vimala’s daughters, transporting them to Kamyavana, where the girls lived in a beautiful palace, always playing games with one another. Whenever it was time for a ***rasa*** dance, by the blessings of Lord Rama, these women also went to Vamsivata and fulfilled their hearts’ desires.

These women continued to reside in Kamyavana, where Krsna would visit them and, from there, draw them into the pastime of the ***rasa*** dance. On one such occasion the perspiration of King Vimala’s daughters created a beautiful lake that is known to the present day as Vimala-kunda. One who sees, bathes in, or drinks water from that lake becomes free of all sins. Moreover, those who hear these pastimes of the women of Ayodhya will also go to Goloka.

It should be mentioned that there is no specific indication that these women of Ayodhya ever became *gopis.* Actually, the fact that they lived incognito as the daughters of King Vimala in a palace in Kamyavana suggests that they remained princesses and that their relationship with Krsna was not of the nature of paramours, even though they did have the privilege of entering the *rasa* dance. Such are the variegated pastimes of the Lord.

**The Gopis Who Had Been Sages**

While in exile in Dandaka forest, Lord Ramacandra, Mother Sita, and Laksmana met a group of sages won shipping Gopala, the Lord of the *rasa* dance, hoping to get His association. Upon seeing Lord Rama with a bow and arrows and with matted hair tied on the top of His head the sages were surprised — the beautiful form of the young prince Rama reminded the sages of the cowherd hoy whom they worshipped with mantras. The sages thought, “Here is our Gopala, but without flute and stick.”

The sages bowed before Ramacandra and offered Him suitable prayers, and the kind hearted Lord offered them any benediction they desired. To this the sages replied, “Let us be as Sita is.”

The Lord was unable to fulfil their request at that time, for He had taken a vow to accept only one wife, Sita. But He did promise them, “At the end of Dvapara-yuga you will all join Me in Mathura and your desire will he fulfilled in the *rasa* dance.”

The sages then took birth in Bengal as daughters of a prosperous merchant called Mangala, whose fortunes did not last. Beset with poverty, he sent his daughters to the home of Nanda Maharaja. There the girls were nicely cared for and given the service of milking cows. It was not long before they had the chance to see Krsna. Remembering their previous lives, they became worshippers of Yamuna-devi, hoping that with her blessings they would become Krsna’s lovers.

One day, Yamuna-devi appeared before the girls and offered to fulfil their desires. Because of being accepted by that dear associate of the Lord, Krsna also felt obliged to accept the *gopis;* thus, when the full moon night of autumn arrived they each heard Krsna’s flute calling them by name.

**The Gopis Who Had Been Pulinda Women**

Sometime after blessing the sages of Dandaka forest, Lord Ramacandra and His entourage continued on to Pancavati, where they lived happily in a simple cottage. In that same forest there lived a tribe of Pulindas, or aborigines, whose women also fell in love with Lord Rama. They took the dust from the Lord’s lotus feet and smeared it all over their bodies. When they came to understand that Rama would take no other wife but Sita, the Pulindis decided to give up their lives. To save the Pulinda women, Lord Rama appeared to them as a *brahmacari.*

In the form of a *brahmacari,* Lord Ramacandra held a stick and a water pot in His two hands. He told the Pulindis, “O women! Do not give up your lives without good reason. Be patient and at a future date your desires will be fulfilled in the land of Vraja.” After saying this, Lord Rama disappeared, hut His words had made an impression on the Pulindis; they decided to live a life of austerity until their time to meet with the Lord finally came.

Thereafter, many generations of Pulindas lived in the Vindhya Hills, stealing from the rich as a means of sustenance. Once, a local king confronted the Pulindas, and they appealed to Kamsa for help. That demonic king sent Pralamba to their aid, and he brought the Pulindas and their families to live in Mathura.

The girls who had longed for Lord Rama’s company took their births in the families of these Pulindas. The girls were very beautiful. By living in Kamyavana they had the opportunity to see Krsna. Naturally they directed their long-cherished attraction towards Him. Whenever they saw Krsna’s footprints on the ground they would smear the dust from those footprints all over their bodies, enjoying transcendental bliss that forced them to think of Krsna all day and all night.

At the time of the *saradiya rasa-lila* Krsna also called upon them with the sound of His flute. And although they were not born into the families of *gopis,* they also joined Krsna’s dance of love and were fully satisfied in His company. From the Pulinda girls we can learn how to attain perfection by worshipping the dust of Krsna’s lotus feet, which is one and the same as worshipping the dust of Vrndavana.

In this regard Narada Muni says:

*niskincanah sva-krta-karma-phalair viraga*  
*yat tat padam hari-jana munayo mahantah*  
*bhakta jusanti hari-pada-rajah-prasaktah*  
*anye vadanti na sukham kila nairapeksyam*

**“Aloof from material possessions and free from past karma, the sages and saintly devotees who love the dust of Lord Krsna’s feet say there is no real happiness in any other place.”**

And in appreciation of the Pulindis, the *gopis* say:

*purnah pulmdya urugaya-padabja-raga*  
*sri-kunkumena dayita-stana-manditena*  
*tad-darsana-smara-rujas trna-rusitena*  
*limpantya anana-kucesu jahus tad-adhim*

**“The aborigine women of the Vrndavana area become disturbed by lust when they see the grass marked with reddish** ***kunkuma*** **powder. Endowed with the colour of Krsna’s lotus feet, this powder originally decorated the breasts of His beloveds, and when the aborigine women smear it on their faces and breasts, they give up all their anxiety.”**

Merely hearing about how the aborigine girls attained the position of Krsna’s *gopi* friends frees one from all sins and increases one’s affection for Krsna.

**The Gopis Who Had Been the Yajna-Sitas**

Having at last gained victory over Ravana and returned to Ayodhya, where He ruled over the world as its emperor, Lord Ramacandra once overheard a low class man criticise Him for accepting Sita after she had lived as a captive in Ravana’s home. Although Sita had been kidnapped, and although Ravana had never even touched her, Lord Rama thought that such criticism would weaken the citizens’ faith in His ability to rule, and so He sent His pregnant wife to live in the forest hermitage of Vasistha Muni.

As king, Lord Rama continued to perform sacrifices. But in the absence of His wife, He had to conduct them with deities of Sita. Every time Ramacandra performed a sacrifice, He would install a new golden deity of Sita, and at the end of each sacrifice He would place the deity along with the others in a special temple. Thus there were many deities of Sita-devi in Lord Ramachandra’s palace.

One day the Yajna-Sita deities came to life and requested Lord Rama to enjoy with them. But Lord Ramacandra declined, saying, “O beloved wives! I cannot fulfil your request.”

The Yajna-sitas asked, “Why won’t accept us? At the time of the sacrifices You accepted us as Your assistants. Why do You act like a sinful person now and reject us?”

The Lord replied, “It is true. I must accept you. But because I have vowed to accept only one Sita, if I accept any one of you, there will be a quarrel amongst the others. If you wait patiently, however, at the end of Dvapara-yuga in Vrndavana I will surely fulfil your desires.” During the time of Maharaja Nanda, cowherd men from the land of Usinara relocated to Vrndavana because their previous territories had become barren from drought. The king of Vraja welcomed the cowherds and gave them a place to stay by the bank of the Yamuna, where they once again became prosperous through the wealth of their cows. Meanwhile, the Yajna-sitas took birth in Vraja as the beautiful daughters of these cowherd men, who were convinced that their families were graced with goddesses of fortune as daughters.

Like all the other girls in Vrndavana, the Yajna-sita *gopis* fell in love with Krsna. As previous manifestations of Sita-devi, they were expansions of Sri Radha, so they approached Her to find out how they could attain Krsna’s mercy. They asked Krsna’s dearmost beloved, “O Radha! Krsna is Your submissive servant. Tell us, what vow must we follow to attain Krsna’s grace in the same way You have?”

Srimati Radharani was especially kind to these *gopis.* She told them, “To become objects of Krsna’s attention and love, you should follow the vow of fasting on the Ekadasi days.”

The Yajna-sita *gopis* replied, “Please tell us the names of each Ekadasi, and the means to properly observe them. Whatever You order, we shall certainly do.”

Srimati Radharani was pleased by these *gopis’* determination, and so She very patiently described to them all twenty-six Ekadasis, including the two additional Ekadasis observed on Purusottama-masa (the extra month of the Vedic leap year). She taught them how to observe Ekadasi, how to hear about and glorify Krsna on that day, and how to break Ekadasi on the Dvadasi day. At the request of the *gopis,* Radha also described various perfections that practitioners had attained previously by following Ekadasi, convincing the girls that this vow was dearer to Krsna than any other. After Radha had blessed the Yajna-sita *gopis* with success in their efforts and departed, the young *gopis* began to follow Ekadasi exactly as they had been taught.

As foretold by Sri Radha, Krsna was pleased by the Yajna-sita *gopis’* observance of Ekadasi; when the full-moon night of Karttika arrived, He called for them, just as He called for all the other women of Vraja who had developed pure loving devotion for Him.

This pastime, which drives away all inauspiciousness and purifies one’s heart, highlights the importance of following Ekadasi. By the power of the Ekadasi-vrata one can attain the highest perfection. Thus Vaisnavas never neglect to follow the vow of Ekadasi.

**The Gopis Who Had Been Demigoddesses**

The seventh incarnation of Krsna was Yajna, the son of Prajapati Ruci and his wife Akuti, who appeared during the period of Svayambhuva Manu to fill the vacant position of Indra, the king of heaven. Assisted by His sons, such as Yamaraja, Lord Yajna administered universal affairs. Naturally, many demigoddesses became enamoured by the beauty of the Yajna-avatara.

These girls once approached Devala Muni for guidance. He told them to go to the Himalayas and perform specific austerities that would one day qualify them to become the Lord’s companions.

When Brahma and the other demigods appealed to Ksirodaksayi Visnu to relieve the burden of the earth, they were told that the Lord would appear to answer their prayers, and that “...the wives *\[sura*-*striyah\]* of the demigods should also appear in order to satisfy Him.”

Thus the wives and daughters of the demigods, including the women who had fallen in love with Lord Yajna, took birth not only in Vraja, but also in Mathura and Dvaraka, as the nature of their individual relationships with the Lord dictated. In this regard Srila Prabhupada writes:

**“*****Sura-stri*****, the women of the heavenly planets, were thus ordered to appear in the Yadu dynasty in Vrndavana to enrich the pastimes of Lord Krsna. These** ***sura-stri,*** **when further trained to live with Krsna, would he transferred to the original Goloka Vrndavana.”**

These demigoddesses took birth in the family of a *gopa* king called Nanda-divaspati who, on Nanda Maharaja’s invitation, moved to Vrndavana with his thousand wives. These demigoddesses-turned - *gopis* naturally saw Krsna as He tended cows in the pastures of Vraja. They recognised Him to be the same person as the Yajna-avatara whom they loved. Every morning these girls would bathe in the Yamuna and loudly sing Krsna’s glories and pastimes.

One day Krsna appeared to these *gopis,* expressed His pleasure with their devotion, and offered them a boon. The demigoddesses asked to be able to see Him before their eyes always, without interruption. Krsna happily granted this request, and thus they always saw the Lord within their hearts. Later these girls would also come to the *saradiya rasa* dance, where their long-cherished desire to be like wives of the Lord was fulfilled.

**The Gopis Who Had Been Medicinal Herbs**

Dhanvantari, a plenary portion of the Lord and the personification of medical science, first appeared when the demons and demigods were churning the ocean of milk. In that incarnation the Lord brought knowledge of medicine to this world, including the proper use of herbs for the purpose of healing.

With Dhanvantari’s appearance many medicinal herbs also appeared on earth. These herbs, each one extremely potent and capable of curing disease, grew luxuriantly under the Lord’s supervision. When Dhanvantari left the earth, however, these herbs became very unhappy, and in their sorrow they lost their powers for healing.

Dismayed that healers of all sorts were no longer able to reap the proper results from their use, these herbs decided to rejuvenate themselves, and thus they assumed the forms of women and engaged in austerities. After four ages had passed, Dhanvantari again appeared before these personified herbs and offered them a benediction. But the Lord’s appearance was so enchanting that they forgot they wanted to regain their lost medicinal potencies; instead they asked to become the Lord’s wives.

As with other such aspirants, the Lord encouraged them to persevere in their austerities, and in so doing to purify their hearts through the power of service in separation. Dhanvantari added, “At the end of Dvapara-yuga, you will appear as flowering vines in Vrndavana. When I enact the *rasa* dance, at that time you will transform into women, and your desire to be My wives will be fulfilled.”

When at last Krsna played His flute on the night of the *rasa* dance, the power of that transcendental sound vibration not only drew the young *gopis* of Vraja from their homes, but it also transformed the creepers that had once been Lord Dhanvantari’s herbs into gopis, who also joined in the *rasa* dance. How intricate and wonderful are Krsna’s pastimes!

The next classification of *gopis* to be mentioned here are those perfected practitioners who joined not the s*aradiya rasa* dance, but another of Krsna’s *rasa* dances at another time.

**The Gopis Who Had Been Jalandharis**

There was once a demon named Jalandhara who was a partial expansion of Lord Siva. Although he was very sinful, he was protected from the reactions to his misdeeds by the chastity of his devoted wife, Vrnda, who was a partial expansion of Vrnda-devi, Krsna’s eternal associate in Goloka.

Since Jalandhara was such a source of suffering for the demigods, Lord Hari tricked Vrnda by luring her into an amorous connection with Him, thus making her husband vulnerable. It was because of this that Jalandhara was defeated on the battlefield at the hands of the demigods.

When the women of Jalandhara’s country, the Jalandharis, saw Lord Hari in person, and when they heard of Vrnda’s intimacy with the Lord, many of them were inspired to dedicate their hearts to Him. Those women who wanted the Lord as their lover heard a celestial voice proclaim, “Worship Lord Narayana with faith and determination, and at some time in the future, in Vrndavana, you too will be united with the Lord as was Vrnda.”

As the celestial voice had predicted, the Jalandharis took birth in the family of one *gopa* called Rangoji, who got into a dispute with Dhrtarastra and was forced to seek protection from Kamsa. Ultimately, Kamsa relocated Rangoji from Ranga-pattana to a village on the outskirts of Vraja called Barhisat.

In due time these Jalandhari *gopis* were married to various *gopas* throughout Vrndavana. Of course they had the opportunity to see Krsna, hear His flute playing, and talk about Him with other *gopis.* The Jalandhari *gopis* could easily recognise that Krsna was the same Hari whom they had loved in a past life. They quickly came to think of Krsna as their paramour.

Although they did not meet Krsna in the *saradiya rasa* dance, some six months later in the month of Caitra they joined Krsna’s nocturnal love festival and realised the inner desire of their hearts. In this way the Jalandhari *gopis* joined the other devotees who had achieved the goal of perfection — Krsna’s company.

**The Gopis Who Had Been Residents of Rama-vaikuntha, Svetadvipa, Urdhva-vaikuntha, Ajita-pada, and Sri Lokacala**

When Laksmi-devi, the goddess of fortune, was born from the ocean of milk, the demigods received Her with a ritualistic bathing ceremony, after which She walked amongst them to select Her husband. But because Lord Narayana is Her eternal consort, She chose Him, much to the chagrin of the demigods.

Along with Laksmi, women from different planets in the universe like Rama-vaikuntha, Svetadvipa, Urdhva-Vaikuntha, Ajita-pada, and Sri Lokacala also appeared from the churning of the milk ocean. When Laksmi became the Lord’s husband, these women, who were Laksmi’s friends, also wanted to marry the Lord.

By Lord Narayana’s blessings those girls appeared in Vrndavana and took birth as the daughters of the six Vrsabhanus. Those young *gopis* quickly became enamoured by Krsna’s beauty and His charming qualities. Realising that Krsna was the same Lord whom they had loved in their previous birth, these *gopis* continued to engage in austerities and were soon rewarded for their devotion.

One day, Krsna appeared to these girls in the guise of a mendicant wearing a tiger skin and sporting matted locks on the top of His head. Although Krsna had disguised Himself, His devotees could not be completely fooled — these girls were naturally attracted to Him, although they did not know why.

The girls asked the yogi to identify Himself. Carefully disguising His voice, Krsna said, “My name is Svayamprakasa and 1 reside at Mana-sarovara. Never eating, I stay alive by My own mystic power, by which I have become all-knowing.”

The *gopis* replied, “If You are all-knowing, then please tell us what is on our minds.” The yogi told the girls to close their eyes. While their eyes were closed, the yogi resumed His original Syamasundara form. Thus, when the girls opened their eyes they saw standing right there before them the object of their long meditation.

Having been accepted by the Lord, these *gopis* fainted in bliss. Not long after, in the month of Magha (January-February), Krsna invited them to participate in the *rasa* dance. Thus their spiritual journey, which had begun at the ocean of milk, finally ended at the Yamuna’s banks.

**The Gopis Who Had Been the Women of Barhismati-pura, the Apsaras, and the Women of Sutala and Nagendra**

The women in these categories took birth in Vraja in different ways, but they shared a common home and attained Krsna’s blessings by adopting a common vow. First I will describe their individual histories and then study what they have in common.

Once, to force the earth to yield the grains stored within it, Prthu Maharaja had the earth take the form of a cow and Svayambhuva Manu take the form of a calf. Prthu then filled a milk pail with the sustenance man derives from the earth and invited other living entities to also take from the earth that which they desired.

At that time the women of Svayambhuva Manu’s capital, Barhismati-pura, became enamoured by the valour and beauty of King Prthu. They approached Atri Muni to guide them to the Lord’s lotus feet.

The sage instructed the women to follow the example of others who had milked the earth for the fulfilment of their desires, as described by Maitreya Muni: “Others, who were as intelligent as King Prthu, also took the essence out of the earthly planet. Indeed, everyone took this opportunity to follow in the footsteps of King Prthu and get whatever he desired from the planet earth.”

Thus, by the blessings of mother earth, the women of Barhismati-pura took birth in Vraja.

The next group of women, the Apsaras, are the heavenly courtesans created by Narayana Rsi to bewilder Cupid. Of these girls, the demigods took Urvasi with them to heaven, but the other Apsaras stayed with the Lord. Naturally, they were enchanted by His youthful beauty and wanted Him to become their lover.

Of course Narayana Rsi was the personification of celibate renunciation; therefore He would never marry. But just to give shelter to His dependents, He instructed the Apsaras in devotional practice and assured them that by its execution they would attain Him when He appeared as a cowherd in Vrndavana.

Another group of women who became enamoured by the Supreme Lord were those of Sutala-loka, the residence of Bali Maharaja. Just after the king of demons had gained universal control, the Lord took birth as the *brahmana* dwarf named Vamana in order to reclaim the planets of the demigods. When Vamana-deva appeared in the sacrificial arena of Bali Maharaja, many of the young women present fell in love with the fair-skinned, fair-haired, diminutive *brahmacari.*

Once again, it was not possible for the Lord to fulfil these women’s desires, even though He continued to live in Sutala as Bali Maharaja’s guard. But the Lord did advise the women to undergo austerities and assured them that their next birth would be as His lovers. This is how the women of Sutala also took birth as *gopis* in Vraja.

In another age long ago, Krsna appeared as the great fish Matsya to save the creatures of this earth from the waters of devastation and to speak the *Vedas,* which had been stolen from mankind. As the Lord plied the ocean, He enchanted Varuna’s daughters.

Lord Matsya advised them to qualify for His association by practising austerities. He assured them that such devotional activities always award favourable results; the girls of Varuna-loka would take birth as *gopis* in Vraja and enjoy the treasures of amorous love with Him.

The daughters of the serpents who served and worshipped Lord Ananta at the bottom of the universe, beneath the planet Patala in Nagaloka, were also irresistibly attracted to the Lord. Sukadeva Gosvami describes this pastime in *Srimad-Bhagavatam:*

Lord Ananta’s arms are attractively long, beautifully decorated with bangles and completely spiritual. They are white, and so they appear like silver columns. When the beautiful princesses of the serpent kings, hoping for the Lord’s auspicious blessing, smear His arms with *aguru* pulp, sandalwood pulp and *kunkuma,* the touch of His limbs awakens lusty desires within them. Understanding their minds, the Lord looks at the princesses with a merciful smile, and they become bashful, realising that He knows their desires. Then they smile beautifully and look upon the Lord’s lotus face, which is beautified by reddish eyes rolling slightly from intoxication and delighted by love for His devotees.

These girls also appeared in Vrndavana along with the women of Barhismati-pura, the Apsaras, and the women of Sutala. They became daughters of a *gopa* called Nanda — not to be confused with Krsna’s father, Nanda Maharaja — who was once a king of Sonapura (in Bihar) but had relocated to Vraja.

Nanda had five thousand wives, who bore him many daughters, some of whom had been the daughters of the Naga serpents. Regardless of their past lives, all of Nanda’s daughters — with the exception of those who were previously from Nagaloka — were attracted to Lord Krsna. Those from Nagaloka, who had previously been maidservants of Ananta-deva, were attracted to Lord Balarama instead.

These two groups of girls — those in love with Krsna and those in love with Balarama — though sisters, cultivated their love separately. They would hear and chant about the two separate objects of their love in two separate camps.

Both groups of girls, however, approached Durvasa Muni for guidance on how to please their beloveds. The great sage advised the girls to follow the fivefold worship of Yamuna-devi, which indeed enabled the girls to achieve their desired goal.

The *gopis* who were in love with Krsna attained Him during the month of Caitra (March-April) in a *rasa* dance that featured a wonderful swing festival by the banks of the Yamuna River. Sri Radha and Her friends were also present at that time.

Many years later — but in the same month — the beautiful *gopis* that had been daughters of the Naga serpents attained Lord Balarama as their lover when the Lord returned to Vraja from Dvaraka. Thus the desires of the daughters of Nanda-gopa were fulfilled.

**Summary**

From the narrations in this this appendix — which show how both men and women have attained the position of *gopis* in subsequent lives, to eventually join Krsna in the *rasa* dance — we can understand the general process of going back to Godhead according to one’s particular relationship with Krsna.

According to *Sri Garga-samhita,* those in an amorous relationship with Krsna go through the following steps to attain ultimate perfection:

(1) The devotee gets the opportunity to see the Lord, but does not closely associate with Him.

(2) By seeing the Lord, such a devotee awakens amorous attraction to Him and desires to establish a relationship.

(3) The fortunate soul then undergoes a prescribed devotional practice in order to purify his or her attachment to the point of being qualified to take birth as a gopi when Krsna displays His pastimes in this world.

(4) Taking birth in Krsna’s pastimes, the aspirant gains the association of the Lord’s eternal companions.

(5) Those whom Krsna deems qualified are called to the saradiya rasa dance, or one of Krsna’s later rasa dances.

(6) Those not yet fully qualified must wait until they are purified further by feelings of separation, caused by hearing from those who associate with Krsna. In this way they too become qualified for the direct company of the Lord.

(7) When Krsna leaves Vrndavana, prolonged separation intensifies the love of His devotees to such a degree that they are finally qualified to go back to Godhead.

(8) By Krsna’s desire they attain entrance into Goloka Vrndavana and become part of His eternal retinue.

## Appendix 32

***The Yearly Festivals of New Vraja-dhama***

*(This appendix follows from the description of Bhusanavana in chapter twenty-nine.)*

In the spiritual world, every day is a festival in glorification of Krsna. The Lord’s eternal associates are not burdened by the struggle for existence that we must endure in the material world; thus, everything they do is in praise of and in service to Krsna. Although in New Vraja-dhama we must attend to our duties of maintenance and preaching, we are nevertheless trying to emulate life in Goloka Vrndavana. For this reason I have prepared a festival schedule that will give ample opportunity for increased Krsna consciousness and constant remembrance of the Lord.

In the following appendix I will first list the festivals according to the lunar calendar and then describe the general characteristics common to most festivals. The balance of the appendix includes a short description of those characteristics unique to the festivals I have added to the Gaudiya Vaisnava holy days more commonly observed.
